writing_topics.instruction:
Last weekend, you had a very special experience that you will never forget. Write a story about what happened. In your story, you should:
- Say when and where the event took place.
- Describe who was with you and what you did together.
- Explain what made the experience so memorable.
- Write about how you felt before, during and after the event.

Write about 80 to 120 words.

Your cousin in the United Kingdom has just started Primary 4. Write a friendly letter to tell him or her about your school life in Hong Kong. In your letter, you should:
- Greet your cousin and ask about his or her school.
- Tell your cousin about your favourite subject and why you like it.
- Describe a fun activity you did during recess.
- Invite your cousin to visit Hong Kong one day.

Write about 80 to 120 words. Use a proper letter format with a date, greeting, body and closing.

Everyone has a favourite place in Hong Kong. It could be a park, a beach, a market or a shop. Write a description of your favourite place. You should:
- Name the place and say where it is.
- Describe what you can see, hear and smell there.
- Explain what you like to do at this place.
- Say why this place is special to you and your family.

Write about 80 to 120 words.
writing_topics.topic_title: My Favourite Place in Hong Kong

writing_topics.instruction:
Imagine that one day you got lost on your way home from school. Write a story about this experience. You should:
- Describe where you were and how you got lost.
- Say what you did to try to find your way.
- Tell the story about who helped you in the end.
- Explain how you felt during the experience and what you learned from it.

Write about 80 to 120 words.

Your English teacher has asked you to write a blog post for the class website about your favourite hobby. In your blog post, you should:
- Give your blog post a catchy title.
- Introduce the hobby and say when you started doing it.
- Describe what you need for the hobby and where you usually do it.
- Explain why you enjoy the hobby and what you have learned from it.
- Encourage your readers to try a new hobby.

Write about 120 to 160 words.
writing_topics.topic_title: A Blog Post About My Hobby

writing_topics.instruction:
You have made a new friend called Amelia from Sydney, Australia through a school pen-pal programme. Write an email to introduce yourself. You should:
- Start with a friendly greeting and a short opening.
- Tell Amelia about yourself, your family and your school life in Hong Kong.
- Describe what you like to do after school and at weekends.
- Ask Amelia some questions about life in Sydney.
- End the email in a friendly way.

Write about 120 to 160 words. Use a proper email format with a subject line, greeting and sign-off.
writing_topics.topic_title: Email to a New Friend from Sydney

writing_topics.instruction:
On your birthday, you received a strange wrapped gift with no name on it. The gift changed your life in an unexpected way. Write a story about what happened. You should:
- Describe the gift and how you felt when you opened it.
- Explain what was special or mysterious about the gift.
- Tell the story of how the gift led you on an adventure or taught you something important.
- Describe how the experience changed you.

Write about 120 to 160 words.

Your principal wants to improve the school canteen. He has asked you to write a short report based on a survey of your classmates. In your report, you should:
- Give your report a clear title.
- Describe the food and drinks that are sold in the canteen.
- Say what students like and dislike about the canteen.
- Suggest two or three ways to make the canteen better.
- Use subheadings to organise your ideas.

Write about 120 to 160 words.
writing_topics.topic_title: A Report About the School Canteen

writing_topics.instruction:
Your school is holding an assembly about caring for the environment. You have been chosen to give a short speech on why we should protect our oceans. In your speech, you should:
- Greet the audience and introduce your topic.
- Explain why the oceans are important to people, animals and the planet.
- Give one or two examples of problems the oceans are facing, such as plastic pollution.
- Suggest what students can do to help protect the oceans.
- End your speech with a strong message that the audience will remember.

Write about 160 to 200 words. Use an engaging tone suitable for a school speech.
writing_topics.topic_title: Speech: Why We Should Protect Our Oceans

writing_topics.instruction:
Imagine that one day you found an old object in your grandmother's attic and it magically took you back in time to Hong Kong in the 1960s. Write a story about your adventure. You should:
- Describe the object you found and how the time travel happened.
- Tell the reader what Hong Kong looked like in the past and what you saw.
- Describe a person you met and what you learned from him or her.
- Explain how you returned to the present and how the experience changed the way you think about your family.

Write about 160 to 200 words.

Your school is holding an Open Day for parents and younger children. Design a colourful leaflet to welcome visitors and tell them what they can see and do. Your leaflet should include:
- A catchy title and a short welcome message.
- Information about the date, time and location of the Open Day.
- A list of interesting activities, such as music performances, science experiments or games.
- A short description of two clubs or teams that visitors can join.
- A friendly closing line that invites visitors to come.

Write about 160 to 200 words. Use short sections, bullet points and subheadings to make the leaflet easy to read.
writing_topics.topic_title: Leaflet for Our School Open Day
